elements.title: Purpose note
elements.content: Explain major developments against the institutional vision and mission.

The policy applies to all e-courses developed by the faculty fulltime faculty members of the FLAME University, and are offered to the internal or external participants.  It is not the intent of this policy to supersede any existing policies set forth by the University, but where necessary, to define new or to expand existing policies and procedures to ensure the most effective implementation and support of e- courses and programs.
Scope

The policy applied to all the regular faculty members, Centre Heads and other academic staff of the FLAME University. The policy provides the guidelines for all e- courses offered by FLAME University, Pune. The policy encourages and enables faculty to develop quality hybrid and fully online courses.
Definitions
E-Course: An e-course is a short duration course content aimed at internal or external audience, with the online delivery mode.
Content: The content is the teaching learning material created for the purpose of online teaching.
Content creator: The content creator is a faculty member with expertise on the subject matter.
Course Duration: The duration of the course may vary from few hours to a term of one month.
E-Course committee
The committee is formed to receive, review, process and recommend the e-course s proposed by the faculty members. The Composition of the committee is as under
Vice Chancellor: Chairperson
Dean of the school: Member
Director IQAC: Member
Dean: Research: Member
Representative of IT Cell: Member
Representative of Library: Member
Representative of Writing Centre: Member
Quality of the e-course
In general, the e-course should adopt the Four quadrant guidelines for content creation for the e-course. The four Quadrant approach means e-course that has the following components:

Quadrant-I is e-Tutorial; which shall contain: Video and Audio Content in an organized form, Animation, Simulations, video demonstrations, Virtual Labs, etc, along with the transcription of the video.

Quadrant-II is e-Content; which shall contain; self-instructional material, e-Books, illustrations, case studies, presentations etc, and also contain Web Resources such as further references, Related Links, Open source Content on Internet, Video, Case Studies, books including e-books, research papers & journals, Anecdotal information, Historical development of the subject, Articles, etc.
Quadrant-III is the Discussion forum for raising of doubts and clarifying them on a near real time basis by the Course Coordinator or his team.

Quadrant-IV is Assessment, which shall contain; Problems and Solutions, which could be in the form of Multiple-Choice Questions, Fill in the blanks, Matching Questions, Short Answer Questions, Long Answer Questions, Quizzes, Assignments and solutions, Discussion forum topics and setting up the FAQs, Clarifications on general misconceptions.
Plagiarism

The content of the e-course should be free from the plagiarism.  A plagiarism report and the recommendation of the Dean, Research is mandatory before conduct of the course.  Faculty who are developing online courses are required to comply with all laws relative to accessibility of course materials. Copyrights and other intellectual property rights of material referred in the e-course. The proper credits to the original authors should be abided by strictly as per the law.
Duration of the e-Course

The duration of the course may vary from few hours to a term. The duration will be decided based on the need, and feasibility of the course under various parameters like, the number of faculty members involved, revenue generation, number of participants etc.
Proposal for the e-course

The proposal for the e course may be made by the faculty member who want to conduct such course. The detailed proposal should be submitted to the e-content development committee. Upon the recommendation of the committee, the proposal may be submitted to the Vice Chancellor/Board for the approval.
Credit compensation

The regular faculty of the FLAME University may opt for the regular credit obligation reduction based on the number of hours involving the conduct of the e-course. The general guideline will be compensation of one credit for 15 hours of e-content delivery.
Credits beyond regular academic load

If the e-content and development id done in addition to the faculty members regular credit obligations, he/she may be compensated as per the prevailing rates of the University for such efforts. But a prior approval for all such compensation will be required.
Eligibility for the e-course development

The faculty member proposing an e-course should be having sound knowledge and expertise in the domain. Normally a faculty member with the rank associate professor or similarly experienced professor of practice/academic experts will be considered for such courses. In the exceptional circumstances, the faculty members of assistant professor ranks may be allowed to conduct such courses. Only those proposals from such faculty will be approved which meet the highest criteria. An ‘strong  recommendation’ from the Dean is mandatory for such proposals.
Responsibilities:

The faculty member who proposes the course will be completely responsible for the conduct and successful closer of the course. He/she may opt for the support form the university, with prior approval form the E-course committee.
Institutional Support for e-Courses

Mostly it is expected from the faculty member proposing the e-course to develop and conduct the course, but due to the technology involved for such courses, the University support may be needed for the successful delivery of such courses. The IT department of the University may be approached for any support needed well in advance. All such needed support should be clearly mentioned in the proposal submitted before the committee for the approval.

Technological readiness is extremely important to the success of any e-course. Inadequate technological readiness disrupts learning and e-Learning efforts and generally manifests itself in course evaluations. It is therefore required that faculty member who are interested in conducting e-course become familiar with the standards and best practices associated with e-Learning.
Faculty Support

E content development is an specialised task. It is easy to underestimate the effort and skill required of faculty to convert from a conventional classroom format to an e-course format. Schools and departments are therefore encouraged to make appropriate resources available for these faculty in order that they might achieve e-Learning-related goals.
Library Support

The Library shall provide the needed support for e-courses development. Elements of library support available may include electronic document, electronic reserves, electronic journals and books, full-text databases, end-user searching, reference assistance and instruction, remote access to networked resources, library resource management services etc.
Copyright, Patent and Ownership Policy

Ownership of e-course material, copyright issues, and the utilization of revenue derived from the creation and production of software, e-Learning courses, or other media products shall be governed by the Intellectual Property Rights Policy of the FLAME University.

FLAME University shall have a significant interest in ensuring that all copyrighted material is protected and that the rights of copyright holders and creators of intellectual property are respected and maintained.

Quadrant-II is e-Content; which shall contain; self-instructional material, e-Books, illustrations, case studies, presentations etc, and also contain Web Resources such as further references, Related Links, Open source Content on Internet, Video, Case Studies, books including e-books, research papers & journals, Anecdotal information, Historical development of the subject, Articles, etc.

Technological readiness is extremely important to the success of any e-course. Inadequate technological readiness disrupts learning and e-Learning efforts and generally manifests itself in course evaluations. E content development is an specialised task. It is easy to underestimate the effort and skill required of faculty to convert from a conventional classroom format to an e-course format. Schools and departments are therefore encouraged to make appropriate resources available for these faculty in order that they might achieve e-Learning-related goals.

Copyright, Patent and Ownership Policy

Ownership of e-course material, copyright issues, and the utilization of revenue derived from the creation and production of software, e-Learning courses, or other media products shall be governed by the Intellectual Property Rights Policy of the FLAME University.

FLAME University shall have a significant interest in ensuring that all copyrighted material is protected and that the rights of copyright holders and creators of intellectual property are respected and maintained.

Quadrant-II is e-Content; which shall contain; self-instructional material, e-Books, illustrations, case studies, presentations etc, and also contain Web Resources such as further references, Related Links, Open source Content on Internet, Video, Case Studies, books including e-books, research papers & journals, Anecdotal information, Historical development of the subject, Articles, etc.
Quadrant-III is the Discussion forum for raising of doubts and clarifying them on a near real time basis by the Course Coordinator or his team.

Quadrant-IV is Assessment, which shall contain; Problems and Solutions, which could be in the form of Multiple-Choice Questions, Fill in the blanks, Matching Questions, Short Answer Questions, Long Answer Questions, Quizzes, Assignments and solutions, Discussion forum topics and setting up the FAQs, Clarifications on general misconceptions.
Plagiarism

The content of the e-course should be free from the plagiarism.  A plagiarism report and the recommendation of the Dean, Research is mandatory before conduct of the course.  Faculty who are developing online courses are required to comply with all laws relative to accessibility of course materials. Copyrights and other intellectual property rights of material referred in the e-course. The proper credits to the original authors should be abided by strictly as per the law.
Duration of the e-Course

The duration of the course may vary from few hours to a term. The duration will be decided based on the need, and feasibility of the course under various parameters like, the number of faculty members involved, revenue generation, number of participants etc.
Proposal for the e-course

The proposal for the e course may be made by the faculty member who want to conduct such course. The detailed proposal should be submitted to the e-content development committee. Upon the recommendation of the committee, the proposal may be submitted to the Vice Chancellor/Board for the approval.
Credit compensation

The regular faculty of the FLAME University may opt for the regular credit obligation reduction based on the number of hours involving the conduct of the e-course. The general guideline will be compensation of one credit for 15 hours of e-content delivery.
Credits beyond regular academic load

If the e-content and development id done in addition to the faculty members regular credit obligations, he/she may be compensated as per the prevailing rates of the University for such efforts. But a prior approval for all such compensation will be required.
Eligibility for the e-course development

The faculty member proposing an e-course should be having sound knowledge and expertise in the domain. Normally a faculty member with the rank associate professor or similarly experienced professor of practice/academic experts will be considered for such courses. In the exceptional circumstances, the faculty members of assistant professor ranks may be allowed to conduct such courses. Only those proposals from such faculty will be approved which meet the highest criteria. An ‘strong  recommendation’ from the Dean is mandatory for such proposals.
Responsibilities:

The faculty member who proposes the course will be completely responsible for the conduct and successful closer of the course. He/she may opt for the support form the university, with prior approval form the E-course committee.
Institutional Support for e-Courses

Mostly it is expected from the faculty member proposing the e-course to develop and conduct the course, but due to the technology involved for such courses, the University support may be needed for the successful delivery of such courses. The IT department of the University may be approached for any support needed well in advance. All such needed support should be clearly mentioned in the proposal submitted before the committee for the approval.

Technological readiness is extremely important to the success of any e-course. Inadequate technological readiness disrupts learning and e-Learning efforts and generally manifests itself in course evaluations. It is therefore required that faculty member who are interested in conducting e-course become familiar with the standards and best practices associated with e-Learning.
Faculty Support

E content development is an specialised task. It is easy to underestimate the effort and skill required of faculty to convert from a conventional classroom format to an e-course format. Schools and departments are therefore encouraged to make appropriate resources available for these faculty in order that they might achieve e-Learning-related goals.
Library Support

The Library shall provide the needed support for e-courses development. Elements of library support available may include electronic document, electronic reserves, electronic journals and books, full-text databases, end-user searching, reference assistance and instruction, remote access to networked resources, library resource management services etc.
Copyright, Patent and Ownership Policy

Ownership of e-course material, copyright issues, and the utilization of revenue derived from the creation and production of software, e-Learning courses, or other media products shall be governed by the Intellectual Property Rights Policy of the FLAME University.

FLAME University shall have a significant interest in ensuring that all copyrighted material is protected and that the rights of copyright holders and creators of intellectual property are respected and maintained.
